questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India states that there will be a Vice-President of India?
questions.solution:
Article 63 of the Constitution of India mandates that 'There shall be a Vice-President of India.'
  • Key Role: The Vice-President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
  • Note: Under Article 64, the Vice-President cannot hold any other office of profit.
  • Succession: If the office of the President falls vacant, the Vice-President discharges the functions of the President (Article 65).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides power to the President for promulgating ordinances?
questions.solution:
Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when both Houses of Parliament are not in session.
  • Legislative Force: An ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament.
  • Duration: It must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of its reassembly, otherwise it ceases to operate.
  • Note: Article 213 provides similar powers to the Governor of a state.

questions.question: The concept of ‘Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People’ is highlighted in Article ______ of the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
Article 330 provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
  • Proportionality: The number of seats reserved is based on the proportion of their population in the State or Union Territory.
  • Related Article: Article 332 provides for reservations in the State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for the creation of a GST Council?
questions.solution:
Article 279A was inserted by the 101st Amendment Act, 2016 to provide for the creation of the GST Council.
  • Structure: It is a joint forum of the Centre and the States, chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
  • Function: It makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, and threshold limits.

questions.question: Who is the ex-officio President of the Indian Parliamentary Group (IPG), set up in 1949, which functions as the national group of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) and the main branch of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) in India?
questions.solution:
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha serves as the ex-officio President of the Indian Parliamentary Group (IPG).
  • Purpose: The IPG acts as a link between the Parliament of India and various Parliaments of the world.
  • Affiliations: It is the National Group of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) and the Main Branch of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) in India.

questions.question: Article 21A of the Constitution of India provides Right to ______.
questions.solution:
Article 21A declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of 6 to 14 years.
  • Introduction: This was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
  • Nature: It transformed the Right to Education into a Fundamental Right.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India adopted Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union?
questions.solution:
Article 343 (1) states that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in the Devanagari script.
  • Numerals: The form of numerals to be used for official purposes shall be the international form of Indian numerals.
  • Note: Article 351 provides a directive for the development and promotion of the Hindi language.

questions.question: According to which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India shall a Money Bill NOT be introduced in the Council of States?
questions.solution:
Article 109 lays down the special procedure in respect of Money Bills, stating they cannot be introduced in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
  • Introduction: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President.
  • Powers: The Rajya Sabha has limited powers; it can only make recommendations within 14 days.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the 'Pardoning Power of the Governor'?
questions.solution:
Article 161 deals with the power of the Governor to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment.
  • Scope: This applies to persons convicted of any offense against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the State extends.
  • Comparison: Unlike the President (Article 72), the Governor cannot pardon a death sentence or cases involving a Court Martial.

questions.question: As per Article ______ of the Constitution of India, English is the official language for all the high courts in the country.
questions.solution:
Article 348 (1) provides that all proceedings in the Supreme Court and every High Court shall be in the English language until Parliament by law provides otherwise.
  • Legislative Text: It also applies to the authoritative texts of Bills, Acts, Ordinances, and Rules.
  • Exception: Under Article 348(2), the Governor can authorize the use of Hindi or another language for High Court proceedings with the President's consent.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Rajya Sabha first constituted?
questions.solution:
The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) was first constituted on April 3, 1952.
  • First Session: Its first sitting was held on May 13, 1952.
  • Nature: It is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution; however, one-third of its members retire every second year.

questions.question: The total membership of the Constituent Assembly was 389, of which ______ were representatives of princely states.
questions.solution:
Out of the total 389 members of the Constituent Assembly, 93 were representatives of the princely states.
  • Distribution: 292 members were from Governors' provinces and 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces.
  • Selection: While provincial representatives were elected, members from princely states were nominated by the heads of those states.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India defines for a separate secretarial staff for each House of the Parliament?
questions.solution:
Article 98 provides that each House of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) shall have a separate secretarial staff.
  • Regulation: Parliament may by law regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to the secretarial staff.
  • Autonomy: This ensures the independence of the legislature from the executive branch.

questions.question: In which of the following states does the Governor have special responsibility under Article 371H of the Constitution with respect to law and order and in discharge of his functions in relation thereto?
questions.solution:
Article 371H contains special provisions for the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Responsibility: The Governor has special responsibility with respect to law and order.
  • Discretion: In discharging these functions, the Governor acts in his individual judgment after consulting the Council of Ministers.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts of the Constitution of India conferred statehood to Goa and formed a new union territory comprising of Daman and Diu?
questions.solution:
The 56th Amendment Act, 1987 conferred statehood on Goa.
  • Daman and Diu: It simultaneously formed a new Union Territory comprising Daman and Diu.
  • Context: Goa became the 25th state of the Indian Union.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Bombay Reorganization Act passed?
questions.solution:
The Bombay Reorganization Act was passed in 1960.
  • Outcome: It divided the bilingual state of Bombay into two separate states: Maharashtra (for Marathi-speaking people) and Gujarat (for Gujarati-speaking people).
  • Significance: Gujarat became the 15th state of the Indian Union.

questions.question: Which of the following is the expanded form of the abbreviation 'Rep.' used in the text of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
In the text of the Constitution, the abbreviation 'Rep.' stands for 'Repealed'.
  • Meaning: It indicates that a particular Article, Section, or Schedule has been officially removed or revoked by a subsequent Amendment Act.
  • Usage: It is often followed by the details of the Amendment Act that removed the text.

questions.question: According to which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India shall a Money Bill not be introduced in a Legislative Council?
questions.solution:
Article 198 specifies the special procedure for Money Bills in State Legislatures, stating they shall not be introduced in a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).
  • Introduction: Like the Lok Sabha, Money Bills in states must start in the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).
  • Time Limit: The Council must return the bill within 14 days.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution demarcates the powers of the Union and the States, that is Union List, State List and Concurrent List?
questions.solution:
The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists that demarcate the distribution of powers between the Union and the States.
  • Union List: Subjects of national importance where only Parliament can make laws.
  • State List: Subjects of local importance where State Legislatures generally legislate.
  • Concurrent List: Subjects where both the Union and States can make laws (e.g., Education).

questions.question: The Indian Forest Act 1927 was enacted after repealing which of the following Indian forest acts?
questions.solution:
The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was enacted to consolidate the law relating to forests and was passed after repealing the Indian Forest Act, 1878.
  • History: The 1878 Act had previously replaced the first forest legislation, the Indian Forest Act of 1865.
  • Purpose: The 1927 Act defines the procedure for declaring an area a Reserved Forest, Protected Forest, or Village Forest.

questions.question: Who has the power to recommend the dismissal of the state government and suspension or dissolution of the state assembly?
questions.solution:
The Governor of a state has the power to recommend the dismissal of the state government or the dissolution of the assembly to the President.
  • Article 356: This recommendation often leads to the imposition of President's Rule if the constitutional machinery in the state fails.
  • Role: The Governor acts as a bridge between the Central government and the State government.

questions.question: Who among the following appoints the Speaker 'Pro tem' of the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The President appoints the Speaker 'Pro tem' of the Lok Sabha.
  • Who: Usually, the senior-most member of the newly elected Lok Sabha is chosen.
  • Function: The primary duties are to administer the oath to new members and to enable the House to elect a permanent Speaker.

questions.question: Through which amendment was the Tenth Schedule added to the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The Tenth Schedule, also known as the Anti-Defection Law, was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985.
  • Purpose: It sets the provisions for disqualification of elected members on the grounds of defection from one political party to another.
  • Note: It was further strengthened by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003.

questions.question: In which year were the Fundamental Duties of citizens added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment?
questions.solution:
Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.
  • Committee: They were added based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
  • Placement: They are contained in Part IV-A and Article 51A. Originally 10, there are now 11 duties.

questions.question: When is the National Voters Day observed by the Election Commission of India?
questions.solution:
National Voters Day is observed every year on January 25.
  • Origin: It marks the foundation day of the Election Commission of India (established Jan 25, 1950).
  • Objective: To encourage, facilitate, and maximize the enrollment of new voters and promote democratic participation.

questions.question: According to which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India can the Parliament amend the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Article 368 provides the power and procedure for the Parliament to amend the Constitution.
  • Types: Amendments can be made by a simple majority, a special majority, or a special majority with ratification by half of the state legislatures.
  • Limitation: Parliament cannot amend the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution (as ruled in the Kesavananda Bharati case).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India states that there would be no tax levied or collected EXCEPT by the authority of law?
questions.solution:
Article 265 states: 'No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.'
  • Protection: This ensures that the executive cannot impose taxes arbitrarily without legislative approval.
  • Context: This is a fundamental principle of financial administration in Indian democracy.
